title: Cohomology of the finite canonical graded convolution
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and d normalized canonical tensor localization data [lem-kun-canonical-tensor-data]. For bounded derived module objects C,D, integers n,a, the module H^n(gr^a(star(T C,T D))) is naturally isomorphic to the coproduct, over pairs (i,j) of integers with i+j=-a, of H^{n+a}(single_0(H^i C) tensor^L single_0(H^j D))) [lem-kun-derived-module-tor-comparison]. For maps f and g, the induced map is exactly the coproduct of the maps from H^i(f) and H^j(g) under this derived tensor cohomology bifunctor. This asserts only a graded cohomology calculation, without a spectral sequence, Tor comparison or convergence.

source.place: Stacks Project More on Algebra Tag 0H7Z, graded cohomology computation before identifying Tor

proof.text: Apply cohomology to d.graded on any finite support. Additive functors preserve finite biproducts, and tensor summands outside the support are zero. Identify the resulting finite coproduct with the coproduct indexed by all integers, using the zero maps on omitted summands. This comparison agrees under enlarging support by the equations d.graded_extension. For maps, pass both chosen supports to their union; d.graded_naturality proves naturality on that common support.

In each summand apply the two components of d.eTgr, the derived tensor shift comparison combining shifts r and a-r into a, and the cohomology shift comparison. Prove simultaneous naturality by the commShift naturality squares and the tensor interchange identity. Thus the summand is H^{n+a}(single_0(H^-r C) tensor^L single_0(H^-(a-r) D))). Take the coproduct of these isomorphisms and reindex by the explicit integer bijection r ↦ (-r,-(a-r)) onto the diagonal i+j=-a. Check the coproduct maps after each inclusion. Compose with the first step; the inverse naturality equation gives the required forward map equation.

theorem kunnethCanonicalGradedCohomology (d : CanonicalTensorLocalizationData R) :
    let P (p q : ℤ) (C D : Bounded (ModuleCat.{u} R)) : ModuleCat.{u} R :=
      ∐ fun ij : {ij : ℤ × ℤ // ij.1 + ij.2 = q} ↦
        ((kunnethModuleTensorHomology R p).obj
          ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) ij.val.1).obj C.obj)).obj
          ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) ij.val.2).obj D.obj)
    let m (p q : ℤ) {C C' D D' : Bounded (ModuleCat.{u} R)}
        (f : C ⟶ C') (g : D ⟶ D') : P p q C D ⟶ P p q C' D' :=
      Limits.Sigma.map fun ij ↦
        ((kunnethModuleTensorHomology R p).map
          ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) ij.val.1).map f.hom)).app
            ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) ij.val.2).obj D.obj) ≫
          ((kunnethModuleTensorHomology R p).obj
          ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) ij.val.1).obj C'.obj)).map
            ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) ij.val.2).map g.hom)
    ∃ eGr : ∀ (C D : Bounded (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (n a : ℤ),
        (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).obj
            ((d.gr a).obj ((d.star.obj (d.T.obj C)).obj (d.T.obj D))) ≅
          P (n + a) (-a) C D,
      ∀ (C C' D D' : Bounded (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (f : C ⟶ C') (g : D ⟶ D') (n a : ℤ),
        (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).map
              ((d.gr a).map ((d.star.map (d.T.map f)).app (d.T.obj D) ≫
                (d.star.obj (d.T.obj C')).map (d.T.map g))) ≫
            (eGr C' D' n a).hom =
          (eGr C D n a).hom ≫ m (n + a) (-a) f g
